Act 1's identity is read from the map screen, which titles it 'Underdocks'. This build ships two acts at index 0 - Overgrowth and Underdocks - and Overgrowth is the default, so taking the default would have replayed a different run. mods.name: Slay the Relics Exporter
mods.role: Exports relic and HUD state for a stream overlay to read.
mods.replay_risk: Reads game state and writes it outward. No content, no gameplay hooks. The lowest risk of the three, and the only one whose purpose is incompatible with changing anything.

mods.name: BaseLib
mods.role: The community modding framework most StS2 mods build on.
mods.replay_risk: Infrastructure: hook registration, config UI, menu surfaces. Ships in lockstep with the game. It adds no gameplay content of its own, but it is a patching framework, so 'adds nothing' is a statement about this version rather than about the category.

mods.name: Hindsight
mods.role: Resumes a past run from a chosen floor in run history.
mods.replay_risk: The one that can invalidate a reconstruction outright. A resumed run has the same seed, build, content hash and acts as a fresh one, so no environment gate would notice - the recording would simply not start where the history says it does. Defended against directly by source.run_start rather than by argument.

Evidence.method: The count is observed: the game's version overlay reads MODDED (3) throughout. The three identities were established by a separate investigation of this creator's environment and are not readable from the video, which names no mod anywhere. Recorded as an inference for that reason.
Evidence.note: The content hash is kept as a separate and necessary gate. It checks content ids contributed by mods that declare themselves gameplay-affecting; it is blind to a behaviour patch and to a mod declaring itself non-gameplay. Naming the environment does not make the hash an environment fingerprint, and it does not by itself establish that these three changed nothing.
